doc.title: Alicia Olatuja interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 9, 2018

title: Saying yes to every opportunity
summary: She relies on her team and believes in saying yes to as many opportunities as possible.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: That’s terrific. Have you developed sort of an inner alarm when something comes, an opportunity in your career and you feel like tempted to do it and then say wait a minute, let me think about this.

Oh man, see I’m not good at that. That’s why I have to have a team to help me. Because I’m always like — my philosophy, even when I was in school when I was singing and performing, was to say yes to everything. I really think you should say yes to as much as you possibly can. Because there’s so many opportunities that you want that someone’s going to say no to. Someone else is going to be the gatekeeper of that opportunity. So if you can do something, just do it. Even if you don’t know if you could do it, do it. I’ve had people say, “Oh I would have done this gig but I don’t do that type of music.” I’m like, “You should say yes and then learned it really quickly and then did the gig.” You have to just say yes. You have to do as much yes-yes-yes as you possibly can until you really cannot say yes. Until you have a conflict. Until you feel like you know what, I don’t think that this is a part of what my mission is. I don’t think that this is the direction in which I want to go. But ultimately I’m more of a just say yes to everything unless you feel like it’s going to take away from another yes.
